about.title: Turlock Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Turlock sits in the heart of Stanislaus County, and its streets carry a steady mix of commuters, farm traffic, and local errands. In 2025, the city recorded 331 injury collisions, with 473 people injured and one traffic death. Public collision records show the heaviest counts along Lander Avenue, W Main Street, Geer Road, and N Golden State Boulevard, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to produce the most reports. If you were hurt in one of those crashes, the days that follow can feel scattered: medical visits, a car that may not be drivable, and an adjuster who wants to talk before you are ready. LawProactive exists to simplify one part of that. We are not a law firm. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Turlock car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing unless there is a recovery, and you decide whether to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Turlock Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Years Sounds Long. It Isn't.
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but claims involving a city or county vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can pin down which deadline applies to your Turlock crash.

items.title: Partly at Fault? You May Still Recover.
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if an insurer argues you share some blame for a Geer Road collision, your claim is reduced rather than erased.

items.title: Protect Your Words and Your Evidence.
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may request a recorded statement early, and you are not required to give one. Photos, witness names, and medical records from right after the crash matter, and a contingency-fee attorney can help you preserve them with no fee unless you recover.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company called and wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are under no obligation to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurer, and it is usually wise to hold off. Adjusters may use small inconsistencies to reduce what they pay. Speaking with an attorney first lets you understand what to share and when.

items.question: I was rear-ended on N Golden State Boulevard on a Friday evening and felt fine at the scene. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: Yes. Soft-tissue and head injuries often show up hours or days later, which is one reason Friday evening crashes in Turlock can feel more serious by Monday. See a doctor as soon as symptoms appear, keep every record, and reach out so an attorney can evaluate your situation.

items.question: What does it cost to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means no fee unless there is a recovery in your case, and you are never obligated to hire anyone we introduce.
